topics.topic: Ownership and non-mutating execution of captured trial-case fit and size validation before fixture copying
questions: Which module performs the authoritative contract-fit and fixture-size checks before copying, and what non-writing capability lets `runs` obtain that answer without duplicating checks owned by `functions`?
Which module owns the fit-and-size decision for a captured case, and how can it be completed before runs copies fixture bytes without duplicating that decision?
How can `runs` complete the `functions`-owned fit and size checks before copying files without duplicating those rules or invoking the mutating add operation too early?

quotes:
Capturing a failed execution enters through
  `runs.capture_failed_execution`, which checks first, in this order, the
  record — an executed function element that did not succeed (M06) — and then
  the run and its spool (A15 rule 5), and copies the spooled inputs; it then
  calls `functions.add_captured_trial_case`, which checks that the record's
  pinned contract version is the one named, the case's fit to it and adds it to
  the corpus (A04 rule 1, M06).

`runs` copies a spooled file into
  the content-addressed area only after every check of the capture has passed
  on the records and the files' facts — eligibility, run and spool, then the
  input fits and sizes `functions.add_captured_trial_case` would make —, so a
  refused capture copies nothing and owner decision 9 holds: the only files
  kept beyond a run are trial-case fixtures.
judgement.why: The first passage copies before the functions-owned fit check, while the second requires that check to pass before copying.

topics.topic: Ownership and workflow for random record-identifier generation, collision checks, and retries
questions: Which module owns random identifier generation, collision checking and retry, and how do the modules that create these five record types obtain an identifier?
Which module owns random-ID generation and the atomic check-and-remint behavior shared by `functions`, `bindings`, `runs` and `effects`?

quotes:
`trial_execution_id` M07, `binding_id` M11, `run_id` M19, `approval_id` M24 and
   `grant_id` M25 are minted at random by the kernel; one that already exists is
   minted again.
judgement.why: The random-identifier requirement and the absence of a named State 3 owner predate the reopening, and the change did not touch or affect them.

topics.topic: Validation and handling of duplicate configured agent names at startup or reload
questions: If a changed configuration introduces two agent tokens with the same `agent_name`, must the next-request re-read reject it, accept it until restart, or represent the two tokens as the same actor?
Which module validates unique agent names and refuses startup when a name is repeated?

quotes:
`agent_name`: for an agent, the name its token has in the installation; names
  are unique in an installation, and a configuration repeating one is refused at
  start.

Exactly three checks apply to a re-read: the
   file can be read and parsed; every token is at least 43 characters; no two
   tokens are equal.
judgement.why: Both the startup uniqueness requirement and the closed reload-check list were unchanged, and the change did not make their ownership or reload interaction matter.

topics.topic: Ownership and intermediate result contract for final service-invocation outcomes
questions: Which module owns the final A09 outcome after response decoding, value storage and spooling, and what result does `service_invoker` return before those later checks?

topics.topic: Ownership and provision of provisional attempt identity during file spooling
questions: Who computes and supplies the provisional attempt identity used by `spool_file` before the concluding NodeExecution exists?
Does `models` own the disclosure-class ordering while `canonical_values` only owns the comparison/highest operation, or does `canonical_values` also own the ordering data?

topics.topic: Ownership of stored-record behavior for equal-content submissions
questions: Which module owns the stored-record behavior for an equal contract, implementation, trial case, flow version or value submission?

topics.topic: Scope of startup recovery for non-final runs, including waiting runs
questions: Does the recovery capability scan and re-derive every non-final run, including waiting runs whose approval or attempt records changed before a crash, or only runs whose stored status is `running`?
